# Independent review: direct conditional Pick bridge

Date: 2026-09-17.
Reviewer: `/root/pairzero_geometry_review`.
Verdict: **ACCEPT_ENTIRE_H_GROWTH_AND_DIRECT_CONDITIONAL_PICK_BRIDGE_ONLY**.

## Exact binding and external-input boundary

Candidate: `KPS_DIRECT_PICK_BRIDGE_CANDIDATE.md`.
SHA256: `2bf161414992d7a50d3bba60c0aa99c18e34a9862bc3c0ecff157411dd4a1239`.
Size: 9339 bytes, 194 LF. The complete final candidate was read.
Declared research base: `8d3a63ae28c1ac92f06f433cd7e1b8d4ec266679`.

Checked project hashes:

- `REPORT_2026-09-17_KPS_MELLIN_DIVISOR_AUDIT.md`:
  `00cb5a4b3739314a8a584469179ee5cc8e72238a48f186f12d28cba2f4383528`.
- `REPORT_2026-09-17_KPS_MOMENT_INTERFACE.md`:
  `8db1503625708a8271f63ea9b1ff33ed5d38ecbe131718ab152688b322e528a0`.
- `PROSHKA_RESPONSE_GOAL058_KPSQUOTIENT_2026-09-17.md`:
  `14dcccc1270d83595d03dfcdb784c0b419e946b8fe2a966bfdaa153d5cd6647d`.
- Its completed independent review `KPSQUOTIENT_RESPONSE_REVIEW.md`:
  `fde1b165acc3fb4adc9ef436b69296af1301e25c60cb0884e53c2cf56ddf8a0e`.

The preceding accepted source normalization, entire real H, open-real-interval
positivity H(v)>0 for v>-3/2, and KQ14 cancellation-independent zero filter
are reused within their stated scope. No actual class membership or source-sign
conclusion is imported from these reports. Their full older archive is not
recursively re-audited here.

Primary authors' PDF:
`Baricz_Singh_1702.00626.pdf`, SHA256
`992a42316a41b39027377cbb2690b908ee14f3c1e2464b23c9727316d882abc7`.
Local text SHA256:
`3f09d27198002e3f9d8107cbc9422738b41e015c66ba9763fd8329398b8d2c69`.
The title/version page and printed pp2-3 were read, including Lemma 1 and
Lemma 4. The title page identifies arXiv:1702.00626v2, 16 August 2017.

**External theorem used:** the classical Laguerre coefficient-transform theorem
as explicitly stated in Lemma 1, p2, of
[Baricz--Singh, Zeros of some special entire functions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1702.00626).
For a real entire A of order less than two with only negative real zeros,
it gives only negative real zeros for sum A(n)w^n/n!. The statement imposes
neither simplicity of zeros nor a unit separation condition. Lemma 4 is a
related canonical-product multiplier statement and is not needed for the
present application. This review checks the exact theorem statement and all
application hypotheses; it does not independently reprove the 1898 theorem
or audit its original historical proof. The published KPS Theorem 4.4 is
not used in this direct transfer.

The reciprocal-Gamma product was also read directly at
[DLMF 5.8.2](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.8.E2). Its normalization is
1/Gamma(w)=w exp(gamma w) product_(k>=1)(1+w/k)exp(-w/k), exactly the product
needed for the growth bound below. This was a direct formula check, not a
new literature or zero search.

## R1: the unconditional entire growth bound

The initial real-axis bound is paid by the full series. The two source terms
have prefactors of order n^4 t^(9/4) and n^2 t^(5/4), with t=exp(2x)>=1.
Their absolute sum is bounded by a constant times
 t^(9/4) exp(-pi t) sum_(n>=1)n^4 exp(-pi(n^2-1)).
The series is finite and the polynomial power of t is absorbed by exp(pi t/2).
Thus the displayed bound for q(x), x>=0, holds without a sign premise on
Fourier zeros. Since s-(pi/2)exp(2sqrt(s)) is bounded above, this implies
|rho(s)|<=C_0 exp(-s) on the complete positive axis. The constant may also
absorb any initial compact interval; it is finite.

Local analyticity at zero was already proved for the actual full source. With
0<R<1 strictly inside that analytic disk, Cauchy gives |a_k|<=B R^(-k).
For epsilon=R/2, the remainder after M terms is bounded by
B(s/R)^M/(1-s/R)<=2B(s/R)^M on 0<=s<=epsilon. No global analyticity of rho
in the s-plane is assumed.

On the circle |u|=n, n a positive integer, choose M=n+1 and write sigma=Re u.
All possible Mellin poles have modulus k+1/2. Hence each denominator in the
finite Taylor correction satisfies
|u+k+1/2| >= |n-(k+1/2)| >= 1/2.
The absolute finite correction is at most
2B epsilon^(-n+1/2) sum_(k=0)^n(epsilon/R)^k
<=4B epsilon^(-n+1/2), as claimed in (R3).

The remainder integral is at most
2B R^(-n-1) epsilon^(sigma+n+3/2)/(sigma+n+3/2).
Its denominator is at least 3/2 and its epsilon power has positive exponent,
so it is bounded by (4B/3)R^(-n-1). This verifies (R4), including the
uniformity at the leftmost point sigma=-n.

On [epsilon,1], s^sigma<=epsilon^(-n), giving the first term of (R5).
On [1,infinity), s^(sigma-1/2)<=s^(n-1/2)<=s^n; integration against
exp(-s) is at most n!. Therefore the full continued D, on these circles,
is bounded by a fixed sum of exponential-in-n terms and n!. This gives
log max_(|u|=n)|D(u)| <= C(n+1)log(n+2). It is legitimate to estimate D
on these circles because none contains a half-integer pole; no maximum
principle is applied to D across the poles inside.

For w=u+1/2, |w|<=n+1/2. In the reciprocal-Gamma product split at
K=ceil(2(n+1)). The finite product satisfies an upper logarithmic bound
by sums of log(1+|w|/k)+|w|/k, which are O(n log(n+2)). The prefactor
w exp(gamma w) satisfies the same weaker bound. In the remaining product,
|w/k|<1/2, and log(1+w/k)-w/k has modulus at most a constant times
|w|^2/k^2. The tail contributes O(|w|^2/K)=O(n). Zeros of a finite factor
can only lower the modulus and do not spoil this upper bound. Thus
1/Gamma(u+1/2) has the asserted exp(O(n log(n+2))) bound on the circles.

Multiplying the bounds gives the same form for H. Unlike D, H is already
entire, so the maximum modulus principle is valid on every enclosed disk.
For r>=1 take n=ceil(r); the unit disk handles 0<=r<1 after enlarging the
constant. This proves
max_(|u|<=r)|H(u)| <= exp(C(r+1)log(r+2)).
Its entire order is at most one, hence strictly below two. No zero-location
hypothesis, RH, Pick premise or KPS unit-gap condition was used in R1.

## R2: exact coefficients and the classical transfer

The substitution s=x^2 and evenness give
D(n)=2 int_0^infinity x^(2n)q(x)dx=mu_(2n), including D(0)=mu_0=1.
The half-integer Gamma identity then gives
H(0)=1/sqrt(pi), and
H(n)/H(0)=4^n n! mu_(2n)/(2n)!.
Consequently G(w)=sum H(n)w^n/(H(0)n!) has coefficients
4^n mu_(2n)/(2n)!, and substitution w=-z^2/4 gives precisely the entire
Fourier series of F. The factor four and both normalization constants are
correct. Entireness of G follows from that coefficient relation to the
known even entire F; a square-root branch is not an additional hypothesis.

Now assume, conditionally, that every zero of H is real. The independently
accepted positivity on v>-3/2 places every such zero in (-infinity,-3/2],
which is strictly on the negative real axis. The possible boundary point
-3/2 is harmless; no removed endpoint-curvature assertion is being reused.
H is real entire, nonzero, H(0)>0, and R1 gives order<=1<2. Division by
H(0) changes none of these conditions. All hypotheses of the stated
Laguerre theorem are therefore met. Multiplicity is unrestricted, and the
case with no zeros is allowed; no extra existence assumption is needed.

The theorem gives only negative real zeros of G. Its constant term is one,
so zero itself is not a zero. If F(z)=0, then G(-z^2/4)=0, making z^2
strictly positive real. This forces z real. Thus R2 is a valid closed
conditional transfer, subject to the named external classical theorem.
It is not a proof that the actual H has only real zeros.

## R3: why the separately assumed unit separation disappears

Assume the exact source quotient phi_*=4H(u-1)/H(u) admits the global Pick
extension defined in the candidate. The independently accepted KQ14 then
excludes every nonreal zero of the meromorphically continued D. This use of
KQ14 retains its finite-forward-chain argument and multiplicity/cancellation
analysis; it is not an assumption that numerator and denominator never
cancel.

At any nonreal point Gamma(u+1/2) is finite, holomorphic and nonzero. Since
D=Gamma(u+1/2)H there, nonreal H and D zeros are exactly the same, with
identical multiplicities. Hence the Pick premise forces every H zero to be
real. The accepted real-axis positivity puts these zeros on the negative
axis, R1 pays the growth condition, and R2 gives only real F zeros.
Finally the exact entire identity F(z)=xi(1/2+iz)/xi(1/2) maps those zeros
to the critical line, giving the claimed conditional RH consequence.

This chain never applies KPS Theorem 4.4 and does not require a separate
hypothesis about the gaps of the surviving phi zeros and poles. The classical
coefficient theorem uses the zero set of H itself, which is why cancelling
chains in the quotient cause no missing unit-gap premise in this proof.
No ordinary Bernstein function is substituted for a Pick function. Real-axis
positivity, finite samples, the parabolic zero-free region or finite order
alone still do not establish the needed global Pick premise.

## Disposition and precise limitation

R1 is accepted as an unconditional additional growth fact for the fixed full
source under the prior accepted analytic inputs. R2 and R3 are accepted only
as conditional transfers, with the classical Laguerre theorem explicitly
external. This is a valid simplification of a sufficient entrance: for this
same quotient, independently proved global Pick membership would suffice,
without separately proving the former KPS unit separation.

The report does not prove actual Pick membership, all-real H zeros, full-V
positivity or RH. It does not claim this sufficient condition necessary for
RH. The older Gaussian-difference BF control and the separate Pick-but-gap-two
polynomial control remain consistent with the argument. No specific prime
property is newly shown to force the missing Pick sign.

No mathematical correction is required in the exact final candidate. This
verdict is isolated PAPER acceptance only, with no canonical/Lean admission,
source-sign delta, source-sign counter reset, proof dispatch or publication.
No source numerical tests, root search or descendant agent were used. The
only written file is this assigned staging review.

# Parent check: direct Pick consumer on the existing H

Candidate SHA256: 2bf161414992d7a50d3bba60c0aa99c18e34a9862bc3c0ecff157411dd4a1239.
No actual global Pick membership is asserted.

R1: The full theta series gives |q(x)|<=C exp[-pi exp(2x)/2] on x>=0,
so rho(s)<=C_0 exp(-s) on s>=0. Local even holomorphy pays a fixed disk
for rho, with |a_k|<=BR^-k. On |u|=n integer, taking M=n+1 Taylor terms
leaves remainder exponent sigma+M-1/2>=1/2. Its integral denominator is
at least 3/2 and its epsilon power at least 3/2. Each removed pole is a
negative half-integer, at distance at least 1/2 from that circle. The
finite correction is bounded by a geometric sum times epsilon^-n.
The tail on [epsilon,1] is bounded by C epsilon^-n, and on [1,infinity)
by C n! using s^(n-1/2)<=s^n. Thus D has exp[O(n log(n+2))] modulus on
these pole-free circles. The reciprocal-Gamma Weierstrass product has
the same bound: for k<=2(n+1), sum log(1+|w|/k)+|w|/k is O(n log n);
for k>2(n+1), log[(1+w/k)exp(-w/k)]=O(|w|^2/k^2) uniformly. Multiplication
and maximum modulus for the already entire H give order at most one.
This is an actual-source growth fact, independent of zero location.

R2: s=x^2 gives D(n)=2 int_0^infinity x^(2n)q(x)dx=mu_(2n), with the
factor 2 matching evenness. H(0)=1/sqrt(pi). Gamma(n+1/2) then gives
H(n)/H(0)=4^n n! mu_(2n)/(2n)!. Hence G(w)=sum H(n)w^n/(H(0)n!) is
entire and F(z)=G(-z^2/4) exactly. Conditional real H zeros are all
negative because H(u)>0 on the real interval u>-3/2. The authors' primary
Baricz-Singh v2 PDF Lemma1 p2 was read in text and visually: the required
conditions are real entire, order<2, and only negative real zeros.
Our R1 pays order, and the conditional premise pays the only missing
zero restriction. That external classical theorem gives only negative
real zeros of G; F(0)=1, so F zeros have positive real z^2 and real z.
No theorem of simplicity, interlacing, or unit spacing is imported.
The named classical theorem is an external input, not independently
reproved by this parent or by looking at its restatement.

R3: Accepted KQ14 excludes all nonreal zeros of continued D under the
hypothetical global Pick property. Gamma is finite and nonzero at every
nonreal point, so H shares precisely those nonreal zeros and has none.
R2 then gives the real-zero conclusion for the exact xi Fourier transform.
This pays Pick => RH for this source without invoking B_P1 membership
or requiring the surviving quotient zero/pole gaps to equal one. It
does not pay the Pick premise, its necessity, any sign via ordinary BF,
or a new source-specific arithmetic mechanism. This is a conditional
consumer simplification; full-V sign frontier and counters unchanged.
